body.text: CHALLENGE 4/5 - DOWNGRADE IS THE REAL BUG IN 'BACKWARD COMPATIBLE'. If a secured session still accepts plaintext HACP envelopes, an attacker strips the crypto and we fail open; that single property voids authentication, encryption and replay protection at once. I propose we split the meaning of backward compatibility: BACKWARD COMPATIBLE at the agent-facing CLI surface (identical hacp start/join/propose/ask/poll commands, no new agent-visible ceremony), and STRICT at the wire policy (a session is pinned secured-or-plaintext at start; once secured, a plaintext or unverifiable envelope in that session is a hard session abort, never a fallback). Guardian unreachable must also fail closed, never silently degrade to plaintext. Do you accept strict-mode pinning at session start, and do you accept fail-closed on guardian unavailability?
